# livekit_api_key (Resource)

An API key of a LiveKit Cloud project, with its secret: the credential servers use to sign access tokens and call the server API. The API has no update, so a change to `description` or `service_account` replaces the key, which `deletion_protection` refuses by default. Needs the admin role (`3`) in the project.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A key for one deployment. Its secret is in the state; pass it on to where
# the servers read it, such as a Kubernetes secret.
resource "livekit_api_key" "backend" {
  description = "Production (GKE)"
}

output "livekit_api_key" {
  value = livekit_api_key.backend.id
}

output "livekit_api_secret" {
  value     = livekit_api_key.backend.secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Refuse to delete or replace this object. Defaults to `true`, because deleting a key cannot be undone, and every server and webhook that uses it stops working at once. Apply `false` before destroying it.
- `description` (String) A label for the key, such as where it is used. Defaults to `""`. Changing it replaces the key.
- `project_id` (String) Project (`p_...`) the API key belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the API key is created; a later change of that default does not move it. Changing this argument replaces the API key.
- `service_account` (Boolean) Whether the key belongs to the project rather than to you. A service account key has no owner and stays when its creator leaves the project; a user's key does not. Defaults to `true`. Changing it replaces the key.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the key was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `id` (String) The API key (`API...`), the public half of the credential.
- `owner_email` (String) Email of the user who owns the key; null for a service account key.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The API secret. The API returns it only when the key is created, so an imported key has none. It is stored in the state.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an API key by "<project_id>/<api_key>". The secret of an existing key
# cannot be read, so it stays empty.
terraform import livekit_api_key.backend p_abc123/APIabcdef123456
```
